title: Scrub operator identifiers from epic branch history before push
description:
One-off, must happen before epic/63t is ever pushed. During this run the orchestrator wrote a Cloudflare account id, a Doppler workplace id, and an operator email into tick notes and .tick/activity/activity.jsonl. The current tree is redacted (placeholders), but the commits on this unpushed branch still contain the originals, and this is a public repo — a follow-up commit does not remove anything from git history.

Do this only when no worker branch is still live on the epic (all tick/* merged, workers torn down), because the rewrite changes every commit id on the branch.

1. Confirm the branch is still unpushed: 'git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD' and no remote ref contains HEAD.
2. Rewrite the unpushed range replacing the three literals with the same placeholders already used in the working tree (<cloudflare-account-id>, <doppler-workplace-id>, <operator>). git-filter-repo --replace-text is the clean tool; git filter-branch over main..HEAD is the fallback.
3. Verify: 'git log -p origin/main..HEAD | grep -F <literal>' returns nothing for each of the three, and the tree at HEAD is byte-identical to the pre-rewrite tree (the rewrite must change history only, never content).
4. Leave main's history alone. Note that the operator email is ALSO present on main already, in internal/tickboard/cloud/client_test.go and .tick/issues/xps.json — pre-existing, already public, and out of scope here; it is covered by the separate repo-wide guard tick.
acceptance_criteria: None of the three literals appear anywhere in 'git log -p origin/main..HEAD'; HEAD's tree is unchanged by the rewrite (verified by comparing tree hashes before and after); the branch pushes cleanly.
